headline: OCD Reports 39,879 Families Affected as Dolphin Reenters PAGASA Monitoring Domain
deck: The OCD reported 132,956 people affected by Luis, Maymay and the habagat as Typhoon Dolphin reentered PAGASA's monitoring domain.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The combined effects of Tropical Cyclones Luis and Maymay and the southwest monsoon affected 39,879 families, or 132,956 people, according to the Office of Civil Defense's August 7 situation report.
At 2:00 PM, Typhoon Dolphin reentered PAGASA's Tropical Cyclone Information Domain, the wider monitoring area used for systems outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility.

sections.heading: What we know
paragraphs: The affected population was reported across six regions: Ilocos Region, Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, Bicol Region, Zamboanga Peninsula and the Cordillera Administrative Region.
Four deaths and one injury were reported. At the time of the report, 6,215 people from 2,021 families were staying in 61 evacuation centers.

Dolphin remained outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility when the OCD figures were reported. Its movement was being monitored because large offshore systems can influence regional weather and the southwest monsoon even without making Philippine landfall.

sections.heading: Background
paragraphs: Successive weather disturbances and the southwest monsoon brought flooding, landslides and transport disruption to several parts of the country. Maymay later weakened and dissipated as a low-pressure area, while authorities continued monitoring rainfall and affected communities.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: Damage assessments, including agricultural and infrastructure losses, were still being consolidated. The reported casualty and affected-population totals may change as local reports are validated.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: Flooding and landslides can isolate communities, interrupt classes and work, damage crops and roads, and force families into evacuation centers. Accurate figures help direct relief supplies and public-safety warnings.

sections.heading: What happens next
paragraphs: The OCD, NDRRMC and local governments will continue validating damage and casualty reports and supporting affected communities. PAGASA will continue monitoring Dolphin and the southwest monsoon for changes that could affect Philippine weather.
